data.rules:
SEASON. Daytime sweeping runs April 1 to November 30 in most neighborhoods. In the North End, South End and Beacon Hill it runs March 1 to December 31. Night sweeping runs all year on main roads, arterials and commercial streets. A posted sign with no months means the restriction is year-round. Source: boston.gov/departments/public-works/street-cleaning-boston (last updated 9/28/26).

The CSV has no per-row season dates, only year_round (361 rows). The March to December group appears to be the north_end_pilot=t rows: South End 192, North End 67, Beacon Hill 61. Two things support this: South End signs read 'MARCH 1 TO DECEMBER 31', and the CDS prototype encodes months 3-12. The flag's meaning itself is not documented, so this is my inference.

DAY VS NIGHT. There are no separate night 'districts'. Night rows sit inside the 25 PWD district codes (1F Downtown, 1T Chinatown, M Multiple, etc.) and are recognizable by their times: 00:01-07:00, 02:00-07:00, 00:00 starts, 05:00/06:00 starts. Day rows are almost all 08:00-12:00 or 12:00-16:00.

ODD/EVEN AND WEEKS. side is Odd or Even (address parity). The two sides usually share a weekday and alternate weeks, for example Odd weeks 1 and 3, Even weeks 2 and 4, Thursday 12-4. 'Week n' means the nth occurrence of that weekday in the month, the same convention as CDS weeks_of_month. The City page says weekly streets are also swept in week 5 and every-other-week streets are not enforced in week 5. However, 113 rows and some signs say '1ST, 3RD & 5TH', so use the row flags, not the page's generalization.

HOLIDAYS AND WEATHER. On listed City holidays, daytime sweeping is canceled and overnight sweeping runs as normal. Evacuation Day and Bunker Hill Day are normal sweeping days (source: boston.gov/departments/311/city-boston-holidays). Rain does not automatically cancel sweeping; check 311. Weekend nights are swept on some streets.

TICKET VS TOW. Traffic Rules and Regulations (March 1, 2025, boston.gov PDF), Art. IV Sec. 1 part 16, prohibits parking where at least one official sign is posted for street cleaning; there is a passenger pick-up/drop-off exception. Under Art. IV Sec. 20(4), street cleaning and snow emergency signs apply to the whole block, even over valid meters. Towing applies only where a sign carries the 'Tow Zone' legend (Art. IV, 'Specific Prohibitions-Tow Zones').

Fines (Parking Clerk fines page, updated 9/14/26, and the Rules):
- Street Cleaning: $40, $13 late penalty. This is the towable daytime case.
- Overnight Street Cleaning (no tow): $90, $30 late penalty.
- Street Cleaning (Charlestown): $90. Charlestown stopped towing for sweeping in a 2015 pilot that was made permanent.
- Overnight sweeping stopped towing with the 2018 Ticket-No-Tow change (City Council transcript, boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/document_files/2018/06/gop_2018-6-1_0566.pdf).

Signs can say 'NO TOW ZONE' (seen in Charlestown in the sign inventory). Towing costs $132 plus $35/day storage plus a fuel surcharge (street-cleaning page). BTD writes the tickets, and private contractors working for BTD do the towing. The posted sign wins over the website or email.

SNOW EMERGENCIES. The Commissioner of Transportation declares a weather emergency (Rules Art. IV Sec. 19). Cars on posted snow emergency arteries are ticketed and towed (boston.gov 'What to do with your car when it snows', updated 2/22/26). The Weather Emergency fine is $45. During declared emergencies, parking is banned on both sides of posted routes. Garage discounts start 2 hours before the declaration and end 2 hours after it lifts. Space savers are allowed until 48 hours after the emergency ends, but never in the South End or Bay Village. Sec. 19 still contains an alternating odd/even one-side prohibition (Nov 15 to Mar 31). City messaging says there is no odd/even side parking during emergencies, so the gap between the legal text and practice is unresolved.

ALERTS TODAY. The City's own reminders moved to Notify Boston (notify.boston.gov/street-alerts, emails from notify@boston.gov). It also sends temporary no-parking alerts for moving trucks, events and construction, so a Boston version of CURB's alerts would overlap with it.
gaps: No published sweeping geometry or segment key. The CSV is linear-referenced (parent route + losta/hista feet) to a PWD route layer that is not public. The City has the joined geometry inside Notify Boston, but that API is undocumented and CORS-locked to notify.boston.gov.

Build-time join is feasible but imperfect. My test matched 91% of rows (3,422/3,758) on street name + cross streets against SAM segments and intersections, and 86% also agree on length within 25%. The remaining ~340 rows need alias tables or hand fixes. Side placement relies on SAM L/R address parity. Unverified: whether this reproduces the City's own block geometry.

Sweeping rows lack season dates, tow vs no-tow, and any holiday flag. These have to be inferred: neighborhood rules for the season, the $90 no-tow cases (Charlestown and overnight), and the HTML holiday page. The CSV has no data dictionary, and the north_end_pilot meaning is my inference.
Same-day cancellations (rain, snow, special events) have no feed.

Parking citations are not published. The newest bulk data I found is a 2018 to Aug 2020 public-records release with issue date and time but no coordinates, plus plates and badges that must be stripped. Boston changed ticket systems in June 2025, so the export format for a new request is unknown.
Meter data looks frozen around 2017: BASE_RATE $0.25 everywhere, no current hourly rates, STREET_CLEANING empty, TOW_AWAY on 54 rows. There are no ParkBoston zone polygons.

No published layer says which blocks are resident-permit-only, loading zones, time-limited or no-stopping. Today that is only available from the raw sign inventory (Boston-specific codes, no public code catalog) or the unofficial, AI-derived CDS prototype API (noisy, no street name or side, last published 2026-05-07).
Snow emergency route geometry is published (segment layer last edited 2011), but there is no declaration-status feed.
The 311 'Parking Enforcement' requests (about 49k in 2026) are complaints, not tickets. At best they are a weak proxy for where enforcement is requested.
License terms are not stated on the ArcGIS layers, the Notify API or the CDS prototype. Only the CKAN datasets are explicitly ODC PDDL.

The CORS difference from SF matters for architecture. CKAN datastore and AGOL send '*', and gisportal/gis.boston.gov echo the Origin, so browser queries work. But the core sweeping data has no geometry to filter spatially, so Boston needs a build step that joins and serves pre-built tiles or GeoJSON instead of querying the City API live with spatial filters.
contactAsks: Publish the sweeping block geometry behind Notify Boston (blockId to paths, variant id = CKAN main_id) as GeoJSON on Analyze Boston. Alternatively, document the /street-alerts/api/streets/* endpoints and allow other origins. This one item removes most of the work.
Provide the PWD sweeping 'parent' route layer and confirm what losta/hista mean (feet along the route, measured from which end). Also say whether parent codes map to SAM ROUTE_IDs.

Provide a data dictionary for the Street Sweeping Schedules CSV: what north_end_pilot means, what null side means (198 rows), per-row season start/end dates, and a tow vs no-tow (Tow Zone) flag per row.
Provide a machine-readable sweeping holiday calendar and any same-day cancellation signal (rain or event suspensions), even as a simple JSON or CSV.

coupling.architecture:
Short answer: the map engine, curb-line drawing, sheet, alert cadence and push delivery don't depend on the city. The SF ties sit in five places: the data source, the time core (time zone, holidays, no seasons), the copy, the baked SF files, and the basemap. Boston's hard part is data: its sweeping schedule has no geometry, so it has to be joined to the city's street segments when the data is built.

1. City config: lib/cities.js, loaded both ways like sweep-core.js (classic script on globalThis plus a Node side-effect import), so there is still no build step. Per city: id, name, short, path ('' for SF, '/boston'), tz ('America/Los_Angeles' / 'America/New_York'), center, zoom, bbox, basemap {url, bounds}, holidays id, season (null for SF; Boston defaults to 04-01..11-30, with North End, South End and Beacon Hill running 03-01..12-31, and year_round rows always on), runtime ('socrata-live' | 'static'), datasets, caps {rpp, meters, loading, whiteZones, enforcement, sweeperPasses, routes, tickets, addressSearch, hoodPages}, fine (SF 105; Boston 40, 90 in Charlestown and overnight), agency names, links (open-data site, re-park rule, report-a-fix), copy strings, and the SEO title templates. Helpers: cityFromPath(), cityFromLatLng().

2. One row shape: keep today's yhqp-riqs row as the shape every city produces ({cnn, corridor, limits, blockside, cnnrightleft, weekday, fromhour, tohour, week1..5, holidays, line} plus an optional season). Then drawSegments, openSheet, nextSweep, sanitizeRule and the /b/ renderer don't change. Ids stay numeric but are only unique per city, so the key everywhere is (city, id).

3. Adapters, split by when they run:
   - Build time: scripts/adapters/{socrata,ckan,arcgis}.mjs are paged fetchers (Socrata with the :id cursor; CKAN datastore_search/_sql with offset; ArcGIS FeatureServer with resultOffset and maxRecordCount 2000). scripts/cities/<id>.mjs combines them into a normalize step that writes data/<id>/{segments,overview,schedules}.json. Boston = CKAN schedule + ArcGIS SAM segments + BPDA neighborhoods. SF's existing scripts keep working and get wrapped later.
   - Runtime: a provider object in index.html with viewport(bbox), byId(id), corridors() and address(q). SocrataLive is SF's current code. Static loads data/<city>/segments.json once and filters in memory. Both return the shared row shape. Long term SF could go static too, which is the direction schedules.json already took.

4. Time core: makeTimeCore({tz, holidays, season}) in lib/sweep-core.js returns parts, wallToInstant, todayParts, today, daysUntil, nextSweep, holidaySkip, seasonSkip, alertAnchors and mornAllowed. The page binds its city's core to the existing sf* globals, which keeps the index.html diff small. Node code calls coreFor(city). Holiday tables move to lib/holidays/{sf,boston}.js, each with its derivation rule and the existing 'fails before it runs out' test. The season check happens inside the scan loop, the horizon becomes about 370 days for seasonal cities, and the watch age skips off-season days.

5. URLs: one origin, path per city. SF stays at the root permanently, because about 12k indexed /b/ pages, the /n/ pages and the App Store links all point there. Boston lives at curb.guide/boston, /boston/b/<id> and /boston/n/<slug>. vercel.json rewrites /boston to a generated static boston/index.html (index.html with the head and copy swapped between markers, like hoods:start/end) and /boston/b/:id to api/block?city=boston. Why paths and not boston.curb.guide: a single origin means one service worker, one web-push subscription and one localStorage per device; the iOS host allowlist already covers it; and SEO authority stays on one domain. Add a city switcher to the info menu. On '/', if geolocation lands in Boston, show a toast linking to /boston.

6. Alerts: sanitizeSpot adds spot.city (whitelisted; missing means 'sf', so every stored watch keeps working). The cron loops stay as they are and call coreFor(spot.city). dueAlert, plannedTimeline and the copy take the city's core, fine and stats. deepLink becomes `${city.path}/b/${id}`. The Redis hashes, the one QStash 15-minute schedule, the Vercel cron and the GitHub backup are shared, since none of them depend on time zone. The saved-alert localStorage key becomes city|cnn|side. It stays one spot per device.

7. SEO pages: per-city schedules.json, sitemap-<city>-blocks.xml and sitemap-<city>.xml behind a sitemap index in robots.txt. The rule for which neighborhoods get pages (lib/hoods.js) becomes per city: SF keeps its citation floor, Boston uses a block-count floor. FAQ copy (fines, towing, appeals) moves into the city config.

8. Basemap: build-basemap.sh and render-basemap.mjs read their bbox jobs from the city config and write to basemap/<city>/. Move the tiles to Cloudflare Pages or R2 when Boston lands; the self-host plan already names that step.

9. iOS: keep one app (guide.curb.ios) and let the web page choose the city. The only native changes are a city-neutral location prompt string and the App Store listing. A separate Boston app would double review work, push setup and listing upkeep for nothing.

10. Operations: the monitor and data-refresh loop over CITIES, with a sample block, tile, coordinates and dataset list per city, and validate-data gets per-city bounds.

Sources: Boston sweeping season, holidays and fines from https://www.boston.gov/departments/public-works/street-sweeping-city and https://www.boston.gov/departments/311/city-boston-holidays. Data from https://data.boston.gov/dataset/street-sweeping-schedules and https://data.boston.gov/dataset/boston-street-segments-sam-system.
coupling.mvpCut:
Smallest Boston that works: the sweeping map plus sweep alerts at curb.guide/boston, with SF left exactly as it is.

Step 0, a 1-day spike that decides everything else: join Boston's 3,758 schedule rows to the SAM street segments (street name plus the from/to cross-street intersections) and resolve Odd/Even to L/R from the segments' address ranges. Then measure how many rows land on geometry. If 90% or more do, the MVP below is about 2 weeks of focused work. If the join is messy, add about a week of manual fixes. This is a rough estimate.

The MVP includes:
1. lib/cities.js with sf and boston.
2. scripts/cities/boston.mjs (CKAN + ArcGIS → data/boston/segments.json + overview.json), splitting multi-day rows into weekdays, flooring 00:01 to 0, and tagging season and overnight holiday rows.
3. The Static provider in index.html, plus root-absolute asset URLs and capability flags that hide the RPP, meters, loading, white-zone, ticket-time, sweeper and route UI.
4. The makeTimeCore refactor: Eastern time, a Boston holiday table, the season field, the longer scan horizon and the watch-age fix.
5. spot.city through sanitizeSpot, the cron, deepLink and the saved-alert key, defaulting to 'sf'.
6. A generated boston/index.html with Boston head and copy, the /boston rewrite, a Boston manifest and service-worker shell entry.
7. A Boston basemap bake.
8. Tests: Eastern-time DST matrix, season edges, holiday table, join fixtures. SF suites stay unchanged and green.
9. One Boston smoke check in the monitor.

Left out at first:
- /boston/b/ and /boston/n/ SEO pages and sitemaps (phase 2, the long-tail growth engine)
- per-block OG cards
- the 'Ticketed ~9:11a' ticket times, sweeper passes and truck routes. Boston publishes no parking-citation data; this needs a records request to the Boston Transportation Department.
- RPP, meters (Boston has a meters dataset, phase 2), color curbs and white zones
- address search (MVP is street-name search, locate and tap)
- the tickets page
- the iOS location string and listing update (the web page already works inside the app)
- about and press copy
- moving tiles off Vercel, unless the deploy size forces it now.

Product risk: Boston already offers its own sweeping reminders (https://notify.boston.gov/street-alerts), and CURB's SF hook (when tickets actually land) has no Boston data yet. Until a records request comes through, the Boston pitch is the block-by-block map plus better alerts.

verdict.summary: I opened all 15 sources plus their APIs and sent CORS checks with Origin: https://curb.guide. All 15 exist and the core picture holds. Three findings matter: 1. **Snow route join is wrong.** The 2011 snow-route segment layer (MapServer/7) does not join to current SAM SEGMENT_IDs. In 399 sampled rows, only 7 had the same street name in SAM. Match those segments spatially or by name. DO_NOT_PARK uses the same 2011 schema and is probably stale the same way. 2. **north_end_pilot is not clean.** It covers 333 rows, not 320, so it does not map cleanly onto the North End, South End and Beacon Hill March to December season. 3. **Better source for temporary no-parking.** Moving Truck Permits has no address field and 13.9% of rows have no coordinates. The AGOL layer Analytics_Street_Access_Awareness_Active_Permits is a better source: it has start and end dates, an estimated length and a SAM address (CORS *). Smaller fixes: - **Meters:** BASE_RATE is $0.25 in 6,947 of 6,955 rows, not every row. The rates page is the Parking Clerk's 'How do Parking Meters Work?' (updated 5/6/26), and its default rate of $2 for other areas is confirmed. - **Signs:** the top codes include standard MUTCD D3-1 and 'NA', so 'mostly Boston-specific' overstates it. 'resident' appears in 185 rows, not 137. asset_status needs filtering because of 4,935 Removed and 3,317 Proposed signs. - **Curb API:** the CDS prototype encodes sweeping months inconsistently (4-11 vs 3-12, sometimes none). Analyze Boston still has no CDS dataset, even though the Curb Lab page (updated 2/11/26) promised one 'in the coming months'. - **Sweeping match:** I re-ran match2.py and got the same result (3,422 matched, 3,220 within 25%). Two caveats: for dead-end rows the length check is partly circular, and the Odd/Even to L/R side mapping was never tested. CORS: - curb.guide can call these directly: the CKAN datastore (*), the S3 CSV (*), the gisportal and gis.boston.gov ArcGIS servers (echo Origin with credentials), AGOL (*), arcgis.com item data (echo) and smart-curb-api (echo). - Server or build-time only: Notify Boston (allows only notify.boston.gov, preflight included) and the wokewindows S3 file (no header). Cartegraph photos send no header, so they work in but not with fetch. Rules I checked against the sources: - **Street-cleaning page (updated 9/28/26):** confirms the Apr 1 to Nov 30 season and Mar 1 to Dec 31 for North End, South End and Beacon Hill. It also confirms year-round night sweeping, the week-5 rule, rain, $132 tow plus $35/day, BTD tickets with private towing, 'posted sign wins' and the Notify Boston migration. - **Fines page (updated 9/14/26):** confirms $40/$13 Street Cleaning, $90/$30 Overnight (no tow), $90/$30 Charlestown and $45 Weather Emergency. The 2018-2020 tickets back this up: code 76 at $40, 340 at $90, 376 at $90. - **Traffic Rules PDF (Mar 1 2025):** confirms Art IV Sec 1 item 16 with the passenger exception, Sec 20(4) whole-block signs even over meters, 'Tow Zone' legend only, and the Sec 19 alternating odd/even one-side rule (Nov 15 to Mar 31, alternating by year, outside the CBD). - **Snow pages (updated 2/22/26 and 3/10/26):** confirm ticket-and-tow on posted arteries, garage discounts from 2 hours before to 2 hours after, and space savers for 48 hours, banned in the South End and Bay Village. I did not find the 'both sides' or 'no odd/even during emergencies' wording on either page, so that remains unverified. - **Not checked:** the 2015 Charlestown and 2018 ticket-no-tow history.
